SEMICON WEST 2026: DAY 1 COMPLETE ANALYSIS (1/5)

SEMICON WEST 2026, DAY 1, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 13, 2026

Moscone Center, San Francisco, California. Event time Pacific.

Coverage: 2,212 posts linked to SEMICON West 2026 in total, of which 2,004 carry a post creation date of October 13, 2026 Pacific time (the balance are thread members and continuations pulled in around the day 1 window). 475 media items are linked to the event, with 366 stored image analyses; 412 media items sit on posts created on day 1 Pacific time. 155 items were flagged on day 1: 9 headline posts and 146 roundup posts across 5 roundups, at 09:24 AM PT (7 items), 12:39 PM PT (9 items), 04:00 PM PT (14 items), 07:03 PM PT (9 items), and a final evening roundup at 10:07 PM PT (7 items). Total roundup items: 46. Distinct authors linked to the archive: 1,489. Every flagged item dated October 13, 2026 Pacific time is covered in this report, mapped item by item in the completeness appendix after Section 9.

A note on sourcing language used throughout: a figure described as coming from a slide photo was read by image analysis from a photograph of a presentation slide posted to X, and is quoted exactly as that analysis recorded it. A figure described as post text appeared in the text of the post itself. Interpretation is labeled as interpretation. Nothing in this report comes from outside the archive except brief, generic framing, and that framing is never presented as a reported fact.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Day 1 of SEMICON West 2026 was, in the archive, really two shows running in parallel, and the tension between them is the story of the day. The first show was the Applied Materials investor breakfast, a roughly 2.5 hour investor presentation flagged in advance by TTradDashboard at 11:00 AM ET and covered live, slide by slide, by BenBajarin. Applied used the breakfast to lay out a 5 year value creation frame, CY25 to CY30, built on 3 claims: that AI computing has started a third great era of wafer fab equipment spending, that the wafer content of AI factories is about to multiply as agentic pods replace generative pods, and that Applied's portfolio, number 1 in deposition, epitaxy, PVD, CMP, implant, thermal and eBeam, with advanced packaging revenue compounding from $0.5B in CY20 to more than $2.4B expected in CY26, lets it convert that demand into margin, specifically +5 ppts of gross margin and +10 ppts of operating margin by CY30, with about 54% gross margin and about 40% operating margin as the 2030 markers repeated across the day's reaction posts. That cluster was the day's only sustained headline news flow besides the morning Semtech and Tower Semiconductor capacity deal, and it produced 8 of the day's 9 headline posts.

The second show was the market's verdict on the first, and it was negative in a specific and informative way. Applied declined to give a single WFE forecast number and declined to give a 2030 top line revenue or WFE target, a refusal documented independently by BenBajarin's slide coverage (the 2030 fan widens with no single point forecast), by lwqbepk, by Invest2Growcom, by TopStockAlerts1, and late in the evening by researchmailbox and 2030FY_X. The stock fell about 6.54% by the midday losers board photographed by teshen8lin, about 7.83% to about $458.68 in Invest2Growcom's print, and 6.69% at the close in the Nodus42 infographic, with 6.7% the figure most repeated. Layered on top of the disappointment was a Citi supply chain warning, reported by teshen8lin in 2 posts, that shortages of DRAM, circuit boards, capacitors and optical components are threatening to bottleneck near term fab expansions. The warning and the missing forecast together turned a bullish equipment morning into a semicap selloff, with LRCX down 3.94% at midday and 2.73% at the close, KLAC down 3.22% at the close, and MU down 4.89% at midday and 3.62% at the close, per the archive's market color posts.

The third thread of the day was memory, and specifically a selloff in memory names that the archive's own commentators spent the afternoon dismantling. The trigger, per the Nodus42 close infographic, was CXMT (https://t.co/fDif8AnFTt) and reported key progress on a 4F2 DRAM cell, with a first product described as a DDR5 server RDIMM by end 2026 and a TrendForce density figure of +30% to 50% from a Shanghai event on October 10, 2026. The rebuttal, built in the jukan05 conversation and extended by Schulz_Research, realmarketmaps, NasdaqTerminal citing Hanwha Investment Research, sem2investor, AppendixZeroAI and others, is coherent: 4F2 at a relaxed 13 to 14nm node is a way to extract more density from DUV because EUV is unavailable to CXMT, it is a commodity DDR5 cost per bit story rather than an HBM story, CXMT's 2026 wafer production may reach 98% of Micron's while its DRAM bit output reaches only 27%, and no verified yields were reported anywhere in the day's archive. SK Hynix closed down 10.1% and Samsung down 7.39% in the Nodus42 figures, a reaction the archive's own contributors repeatedly characterized as excessive relative to the underlying claim. Whether that characterization is right is interpretation; that it was the dominant expert reaction inside the archive is a fact of the record.

The fourth thread was the equipment outlook beyond Applied. A SEMI 2026 fab equipment forecast of $149B, first posted by RanjitAlpha as a raise from $142B with memory equipment growth of 32%, spent most of the day as the report's clearest single source item, and then gained a second, independent report late in the evening when Moonquakes_ai posted that SEMI released a forecast at SEMICON West on October 13 putting 2026 global 12 inch fab front end equipment spending at $149B, up 31%, rising to $227B in 2029, with 20 new 12 inch fabs expected this year. The headline $149B figure is therefore corroborated by 2 accounts reporting the same SEMI release; the from $142B raise framing and the 32% memory equipment growth figure still trace to RanjitAlpha alone, and no primary SEMI release text and no SEMIAmericas post carrying the figure appears in the archive. Around that forecast sat a consistent bullish equipment chorus: LIWEI_TWCapital's fab expansion thread naming AMAT, LRCX, KLAC and ASML as the 4 core names, Schulz_Research's detailed ASML capacity work (low NA EUV about 65 units of capacity in 2026, about 85 planned for 2027, about 110 under investigation for 2028, gated by Carl Zeiss SMT as sole optics supplier), and SingularityRes closing the day with bank estimates for TSMC 2027 capex of $75B (Morgan Stanley), $85B (Goldman), $90B (UBS) and $90B to $100B (Cantor) against a 2026 guide of $60B to $64B.

The fifth thread was optics, and it is where SEMICON West day 1 and OCP Global Summit day 2 physically merged, because the same analysts walked both floors. The archive carries a full co-packaged optics and near packaged optics debate: insane_analyst's NPO first slide set, BenBajarin's photos of a working Ayar Labs CPO demo with live TeraPHY telemetry (extinction ratio 4.01 dB, OMA 374.2 uW, die temperature 53.4 C) whose outbound was still pluggables, the Wiwynn CPO AI Rack placard (64 XPU compute rack architecture, with AyarLabs and Corning), SemiAnalysis on coherent lite for campus links of 5 km or more, Schulz_Research on Linktel's 1.6T CWDM reach limits (under 3 km for standard modules, 800G capped at 10 km), a Semtech versus Macom comparison built around a retimer free active copper slide featuring the Ciena Nitro chip, and, in the final digest, PhotonCap on Lightmatter Passage CPO systems and on 400G per lane pluggable optics plans from NVDA and CSCO. The through line, stated as interpretation, is that day 1 produced no resolution between pluggables, active copper, NPO and CPO; it produced evidence that all 4 are being built, demoed and argued about simultaneously, with serviceability and fiber attach yield as the recurring practical objections to the most integrated options.

The sixth thread was the official show itself, and it was not filler. SEMI opened with a champagne toast to $1 trillion in industry revenue reached 4 years ahead of projections, a CEO Summit keynote from Lalitha Immaneni of Intel Foundry, and an appearance by San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie (all SEMIAmericas). The Geopolitical Summit ran Tuesday 1:30 to 3:30 PM PT with a keynote from Brandon Remington of the International Trade Administration and a fireside with Tim Archer of Lam Research and Representative Darrell Issa. Kulicke and Soffa received the 2026 SEMI Award for North America for advancements in thermo compression bonding. Applied unveiled its EPIC Center collaborative innovation facility in Silicon Valley. Arizona brought more than 30 partners, Mexico issued a formal delegation statement, and a Dominican Republic delegation met with more than 20 US companies and its minister, Eduardo Sanz Lovaton, supplied the archive's photos of the opening keynotes by Joe Stockunas, president of SEMI Americas, and Ajit Manocha, president and CEO of SEMI, whose outlook session was titled Industry Highlights and Outlook to 2035. The Best of West finalists were announced, with the winner to be named Thursday, October 15, 2026, though the archive's announcement graphic carries no finalist names, a gap flagged in Section 9.

The day's net, as interpretation: the fundamental equipment story told on stage (wafer intensity per AI pod up 2x to 4x, packaging revenue compounding, a $149B equipment year, TSMC capex estimates rising into 2027) and the market story told on the tape (no near term number from Applied, sub component bottlenecks per Citi, a memory selloff on an unproven CXMT cell claim) point in opposite directions only if the horizon is the next quarter. On the archive's own evidence, every disagreement on day 1 was about timing and proof, not about direction. That is exactly why the verification ledger in Section 8 matters: the claims most likely to move positions, the $149B forecast details, the CXMT density claim, the memory despec commentary from the Applied Q and A, and the Rubin InferenceX preview multiple in the final roundup, are also the claims with the thinnest or most contested sourcing in the archive.

2. SEMICAP EQUIPMENT AND THE WFE OUTLOOK

2.1 THE APPLIED MATERIALS INVESTOR BREAKFAST: SETUP AND VALUE CREATION TARGETS

Source accounts: BenBajarin (live slide coverage), with advance notices from TTradDashboard and ttvresearch, and an expectations post from BenBajarin.

TTradDashboard posted at 13:03 UTC that the Applied Materials Investor Breakfast Presentation at SEMICON West was scheduled for Tuesday, October 13 at 11:00 AM ET, that the executive team would present to investors for about 2.5 hours, and that a possible update to the WFE outlook and AI driven demand commentary was expected; the post carried an event card graded 5 of 10, investor day. ttvresearch posted at 14:50 UTC that AMAT was 10 minutes from taking the stage. BenBajarin, posting from the room at 14:56 UTC, set the expectations frame that the rest of the day kept returning to: a big week with ASML earnings and TSMC reporting, where ASML likely raises machine estimates and TSMC increases capex, because the semiconductor buildout required to power the future of compute is in full force. A third party comment from MoneyL615 in that thread added that TSMC capex guidance would get the headlines but ASML's order intake mix is the real tell of the week, with a skew toward EUV meaning the AI buildout is still accelerating rather than just holding the line.

The breakfast's first headline item, at 15:24 UTC, covered 2 BenBajarin posts. The first, posted 15:13 UTC, reported CEO Gary Dickerson on the biggest innovation factors driving WFE growth, particularly yield innovation and the emphasis on good chips per wafer (the post text spells the surname Dickinson; the slide analysis and the day's other reporting use Dickerson, which this report follows). The slide photo analysis records the frame slide, titled in substance Opportunities x Applied Advantages = Value Creation. Opportunities, as recorded: AI is fueling a new growth era for wafer fab equipment; the AI roadmap is driven by advances in leading edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging, where Applied is number 1 in process equipment; concurrent races for AI technology leadership and incremental fab capacity expand Applied's addressable opportunities in systems and services. Advantages, as recorded: materials innovation (the most comprehensive enabling technology portfolio for AI compute innovation), integration innovation (co optimized and integrated solutions), and yield innovation (highest resolution imaging plus the most enabling and connected services), all accelerated by the EPIC co innovation platform. The value creation targets, CY25 to CY30, recorded from the slide photo: more than +2 ppts of wafer fab equipment share, +20% service revenue per tool, +5 ppts gross margin, +10 ppts operating margin.

Those 4 targets are the hardest numbers Applied gave all day, and the archive shows they were received 2 ways at once. sphinx_thesis restated them as about 54% gross margin and about 40% operating margin targeted by 2030, and added that leading edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging will drive about 75% of WFE growth through 2030, a figure whose slide basis is the pod content work in Section 3. The Arabic language summary by H_ALHOTHAIFI recorded the same 54% and 40% targets, services revenue above $12B, and up to 100% of free cash flow returned to shareholders, alongside a caution list: no revenue or EPS target, a price of $464.12 against a prior close of $497.53 in the post text, market cap $368B, and a P/E described as 40.0x now and 25.1x on expected 2027 EPS of $18.48, with analyst targets averaging $635.33. Those valuation figures trace to that single infographic and its cited sources (the Applied October 13 investor release, the Q3 FY26 release, StockAnalysis) and are flagged in the ledger as single source within the archive.

2.2 THE WFE SPENDING SLIDE: A 14% CAGR ERA AND A 2030 FAN TO ROUGHLY $600B

Source account: BenBajarin, post at 15:15 UTC, slide photo.

BenBajarin's post text is the context: AMAT not wanting to give a WFE forecast, we have our own, but WFE to the moon visualized. The slide photo analysis records the slide title as AI Computing Drives New Era for Wafer Fab Equipment Spending, sourced on the slide to SEMI, TechInsights and Applied Materials, with WFE spending from 1990 to 2030F in 3 inflections. Inflection 1: the 200mm to 300mm transition, 19% CAGR in the 1990s. Inflection 2: traditional Moore's Law to the PPACt playbook, 0% CAGR in the 2000s, then 14% CAGR from about 2014 to 2026. Inflection 3: AI Computing at Scale, with a forecast fan to 2030F widening up to roughly $600B (the top of the fan as recorded at the time) and no single point forecast given. The factors listed for Inflection 3 on the slide: fab space, energy for data centers, supply chain scaling, and value pricing.

Two things about this slide matter for reading the whole day. First, the 14% CAGR is presented as the description of the era already running from about 2014 to 2026, not as a new forecast, so any use of 14% as Applied's forward WFE growth forecast goes beyond what the slide photo supports. Second, the refusal to pin a single 2030 number is not an omission in one post; it is the consistent record across the slide photo, the reaction posts, and the late evening fragments, where researchmailbox wrote that Applied's comments during the SEMICON West presentation hit AMAT, MU and KLAC, listing first the refusal to provide a 2030 top line revenue or WFE target after investors came into the event expecting a comprehensive 2030 financial model, and 2030FY_X wrote that the stock fell sharply after Dickerson refused to provide a WFE outlook, saying only that demand would be very large, while giving 2030 targets of about 54% non GAAP gross margin (about 100 bps of improvement per year) and about 40% operating margin. Interpretation: Applied gave investors a margin story and a direction story and deliberately withheld a sizing story, and the day's selloff was the price of that withholding, not a rejection of the margin story, which no post in the archive disputes on its own terms.

2.3 THE PORTFOLIO SLIDE: WFE MIX AND SHARE POSITIONS

Source account: BenBajarin, post at 15:40 UTC, slide photo. Post text: AMAT has strong share, and it should grow, in all key segments of WFE, with interesting eBeam in optical work brewing.

The slide, titled Industry's Most Comprehensive and Connected Portfolio (Applied Materials External, based on 2026 estimates and TechInsights WFE subcategory definitions), records WFE mix by segment and Applied's position: Deposition 23% of WFE (ALD check mark, CVD number 1, ECD check mark, Epitaxy number 1, PVD number 1; about 2.5x the nearest competitor). Etch 19% (conductor etch check mark, dielectric etch check mark; leader in conductor etch for advanced foundry logic and DRAM). Materials Modification and Treatments 15% (Cleans partner, CMP number 1, Implant number 1, Thermal number 1; more than 2x the nearest competitor, with a footnote that the figure does not include revenue from partnership agreements). Metrology and Inspection 15% (eBeam number 1, Optical check mark; about 2x the nearest competitor in eBeam, highest resolution imaging). Lithography 29% (lithography check mark in packaging; Track blank). The slide footer: Enables Us to See and Address Most Valuable Opportunities on Roadmap.

Read together with the value creation slide, the portfolio slide is the evidentiary base for the +2 ppts WFE share target: the claimed share gains have to come from segments where Applied is already number 1 or a check mark contender, because lithography, the single largest segment at 29% of WFE, is the segment where the slide claims the least. That is interpretation, but it is interpretation the slide layout itself invites, and it connects directly to Schulz_Research's ASML work in Section 4, where the lithography segment's economics are shown accruing to ASML and Zeiss rather than to Applied.

2.4 THE MATERIALS, WIRING AND DIE SIZE SLIDES

Source account: BenBajarin, posts at 15:49, 15:53 and 15:57 UTC, with the packaging post covered in Section 3.

GAA materials slide (post text: I love this visual so much, Every angstrom matters). The slide photo analysis records: Example, Applied's Unique Materials Capabilities Enable GAA Transistors; a gate all around transistor structure showing silicon nanosheet, gate oxide and metal gate; increasing process complexity at interfaces, with in just about 10nm between nanosheets there are more than 5 distinct materials at 1 to 2nm per layer of material.

Wiring and integration slide (post text: wiring consumes about 50% of chip power; the monolithic design era did not demand the same need for innovation in semicap; pushing the reticle limits is why WFE to the moon). The slide photo analysis records: Integration Reduces Wiring Resistance; wiring consumes about 50% of chip power; the Endura CuBS IMS integrated system (ALD, CVD, PVD, Reflow, Treat) gives 40% lower resistance from 5nm to 1.4nm, per Applied internal data on via contact resistance; more than $3B of CY26 expected revenue for Endura CuBS integrated systems; integrated solutions have grown from about 20% to more than 30% of Applied's systems revenue. The more than $3B CY26 figure is one of only 2 product level CY26 revenue figures in the day's headline flow, the other being the more than $1B HBM packaging figure in Section 3, and both trace to slide photos from a single reporter's posts, a sourcing concentration the ledger records.

Larger dies slide (post text: a visual for the point that mobile was sort of boring for semis; node shrinks were cool but pushing reticle limits is cooler). The slide photo analysis records: AI Workloads Drive Larger Dies, More Transistors and Wiring Layers; examples Mobile Apple A20 Pro 2nm WMCM 2026, AI Training AMD MI455X 2 and 3nm 3.5D 2026, Agentic XPU 3.5D about 2028E. Logic silicon area per package: Mobile 98 mm2, AI training 3,470 mm2, Agentic (estimated) 7,000+ mm2, about 70x mobile. Transistors per package: Mobile 25B, AI training 320B, Agentic about 500B+, about 20x. Copper wiring layers per package: Mobile 17 layers, AI training more than 45 layers, Agentic 55+ layers, about 3x. Sources printed on the slide: TechInsights, AMD, Broadcom (2026), Applied analysis; the agentic figures are a roadmap estimate. The 7,000+ mm2 and 500B+ transistor figures are estimates for a roughly 2028E design, not products, and the ledger files them as company roadmap estimates from a slide photo.

2.5 THE SEMI 2026 FORECAST: $149B

Source accounts: RanjitAlpha (first report, 16:03 UTC, flagged single source and uncorroborated by the SEMI account at the time); Moonquakes_ai and ichi_1111_1111 (late evening).

RanjitAlpha's post text, in full substance: SEMI raises its 2026 fab equipment spending forecast to $149B, up from $142B; memory equipment growth is projected at 32%; bullish for AMAT, LRCX, KLAC and ASML, yet all remain under selling pressure. This was flagged explicitly at the time as single source and uncorroborated by the SEMI account, and that flag was correct on the archive as it stood at 09:24 AM PT.

The position changed in the final evening roundup. Moonquakes_ai, posting at 03:06 UTC on October 14 (08:06 PM PT on October 13), wrote in Chinese that on October 13 SEMI released its latest forecast at SEMICON West: 2026 global 12 inch fab front end equipment spending is expected to reach $149B, up 31% year over year; by 2029 the figure could rise further to $227B; and 20 new 12 inch fabs are expected globally this year (the post text is truncated in the archive at that point). ichi_1111_1111, posting in Japanese at 03:30 UTC, reported that SEMI announced at a pre show briefing for SEMICON West 2026 that the equipment market (in the Americas framing of the post) would double in 3 years, with demand pulled by new US fab construction; no dollar figure appears in that post.

The ledger treatment follows from those texts. The $149B headline for 2026 is confirmed in the limited sense that 2 independent accounts report SEMI releasing that figure at SEMICON West on October 13; it is not confirmed by any primary SEMI document inside the archive, and the 2 reports do not describe the same aggregate in the same words (fab equipment spending in RanjitAlpha; 12 inch fab front end equipment spending, up 31%, in Moonquakes_ai). The raise from $142B, and the 32% memory equipment growth figure, remain single source (RanjitAlpha only). The $227B 2029 figure and the 20 new fabs figure are single source (Moonquakes_ai only). Section 9 sets out what would settle each of these on day 2.

2.6 THE CITI SUPPLY CHAIN WARNING

Source account: teshen8lin, 2 posts, 15:51 and 16:13 UTC. No second account in the archive independently reports the Citi warning in its own words; ayoosignal refers to reported Citi caution on component shortages slowing the pace of equipment investment, which is a reference to the same circulating report rather than an independent sourcing of Citi.

First post text: Citi analysts flagged critical supply chain constraints, such as DRAM memory, circuit boards, capacitors and optical components, that are threatening to bottleneck near term factory expansions. Second post text: shortages of crucial sub components, such as DRAM memory, circuit boards, capacitors and optical components, are threatening to bottleneck near term factory expansions, and this spooked the AI boom casino investors, with LRCX, AMAT and SNDK tagged. The second post's photo is a midday biggest losers screenshot timed 12:11 PM EDT, recorded in the image analysis as: SNDK 1,450.66, down 2.47%; LITE 970.00, down 2.55%; ALAB 315.21, down 2.75%; TTWO 202.60, down 2.98%; SPCX 158.03, down 3.30%; CDNS 335.97, down 3.57%; LRCX 297.37, down 3.94%; SKHY (SK hynix) 155.38, down 4.22%; MU 940.69, down 4.89%; AMAT 465.00, down 6.54%.

今晚20:30，美国9月CPI即将公布！这可能是决定$QQQ、$MU、$SNDK、$NVDA能否迎来一轮超跌反弹的重要催化剂。

先看华尔街目前的预期：CPI同比3.6%，环比0.6%，核心CPI同比2.5%，环比0.2%。乍一看，整体通胀从上个月的3.4%重新升至3.6%，似乎不是好消息，但真正值得关注的反而是核心CPI环比预计从0.3%回落到0.2%。

为什么？因为这次总体通胀回升，很大程度上受到能源价格上涨的影响。相比汽油价格上涨，华尔街更加担心的是通胀重新向住房、服务和其他商品扩散。如果核心CPI能够维持温和增长，美联储继续加息的紧迫性就可能下降。

我目前更倾向于三种情景：25%的主观概率低于预期，50%符合预期，25%高于预期。这不是统计模型，而是我根据当前信息作出的交易情景判断。

如果核心CPI环比低于0.2%，对近期严重超卖的半导体和存储股可能是一次不错的反弹催化剂。如果符合预期，市场也未必会跌，因为近期AI硬件板块已经消化了大量悲观情绪。真正需要警惕的是核心CPI重新达到0.3%甚至更高，导致美债收益率再次明显上行。

还有一点值得关注，今天$ASML公布的财报再次证明，全球先进半导体设备需求依然强劲。也就是说，至少从上游设备订单来看，AI产业链并没有突然停止投资。

但我依然不认为一份CPI就足以改变存储目前的技术结构。$MU、$SNDK短期经历连续调整之后，确实存在超跌反弹需求，可整体K线依然偏弱，中期震荡下行压力尚未解除。

我的判断没有改变：短线看反弹，中期尊重调整趋势，长期依然看好存储基本面。

今晚最值得盯的不是CPI同比涨了多少，而是核心CPI有没有超预期，以及数据公布之后美债收益率会怎么走。

如果核心通胀温和、美债收益率回落，再叠加ASML的基本面利好，半导体就有机会迎来一轮情绪修复。但反弹能走多远，最终还是要看资金愿不愿意重新买入。

Hermes yesterday: 512 commits hit main, more than double any day this series has covered, and the release was cut right behind them: v0.22.0 stable shipped overnight from the day's last commit. The headline: a fresh Desktop install now opens a setup chat, and the free model turns into a one-time trial for it. Here are the 10 that matter.

1️⃣ A fresh Desktop install opens a setup chat

Before: first-run setup lived in a separate hermes-setup profile, started with /initiate-setup, asked its questions on generic cards and handed off to a new chat at the end. After: a fresh Desktop install opens one chat in the default profile that walks through your name, an accent color, a layout, apps to connect, plugins, a quick tour and up to four first tasks picked for you, one card per step; typing in the composer answers the waiting card. Skip setup ends it, closing the app midway starts it over on the next launch, and Settings > Run onboarding again replays it on your configured model. Along the way the agent gained set_theme (it replaces apply_layout), so make it violet, dark mode works in any Desktop chat, and manage_connections can show a browsable connector directory card. Heads-up: /initiate-setup is gone on every surface, and an existing hermes-setup profile stays as an ordinary profile.

2️⃣ The free model becomes a one-time Desktop trial

Before: only the Microsoft Store build had the free model, and there it was on for the whole process: every CLI, gateway and backend boot created an anonymous Nous account, even with another provider configured, and any guest account could run inference. After: the free nous/welcome model is a one-time trial for the first Desktop install of an OS user who never used Hermes on that computer, on any bundle, and only on the Desktop's local backend. The CLI, TUI and messaging gateway no longer create an account at boot or offer the free model; connectors still create their connectors-only identity on first use. Desktop guests that already chatted on the free model keep it, a lost trial (signed in, auth.json deleted) is never claimed again, and the split between trial and connector guests is enforced on the client until a server-side check lands.

3️⃣ Memory edits stop wiping neighboring facts

Before: to change one fact, the memory tool's replace rewrote the whole entry, and models often dropped the other facts in it: NVIDIA measured Opus 4.8 doing it in 19 of 40 tasks. A write without a target fell back to MEMORY.md, so user facts could land there. After: replace is gone and patch is the only edit: it changes exactly one span inside an entry and keeps the rest (1 of 40 in the same test), and a span that appears twice is refused with a request for more context. Every write needs a top-level target. Writes staged for approval before the change still replay, and external memory providers receive a patch as a whole-entry replace. Heads-up: patch does not yet match a span retyped with straight quotes, a plain dash or re-wrapped lines where the entry has the original; a fix is in review.

4️⃣ Stable installs stay on stable

Before: rerunning the installer moved a stable install back to main, because Hermes-Setup bakes --branch main, and its update mode dropped the channel the Desktop asked for. The update check then offered an older stable release as a new update. After: an installer rerun keeps an install whose recorded channel is not main where it is and leaves the move to hermes update, and Hermes-Setup forwards the channel. When the checkout is newer than the chosen stable release, Desktop, hermes update --check, hermes --version and the dashboard call it a rollback (Roll back to v0.21.7) instead of an update. Installs with no channel record, a main record or an explicit --commit behave as before. Not run for real yet: the macOS Hermes-Setup app; the Windows installer is covered by CI tests only.

5️⃣ Connector tools send and save real files

Before: a connector tool that takes a file, like a mail attachment or a drive upload, asked the model for a storage key only the tool gateway can create, so every such call failed, and files a tool returned came back as storage links that expire in about an hour. After: the model passes a local path; Hermes checks it, uploads it (up to 20 MB) and runs the tool, and returned files are saved under downloads/connectors in the Hermes home, where the model can send them on with MEDIA:. Which files may leave follows the MEDIA: rule: on a default install any regular file outside the credential and system denylist, in strict mode (gateway.strict) only caches, allowed folders and recent files. SSH, Modal and other remote terminal backends are refused, downloads stay until you delete them, and the PR's live checks against the real gateway were listed without results when it merged.

6️⃣ A dead MCP login stops hammering the server

Before: an OAuth MCP server whose refresh token was rejected re-sent that dead token on every new session (Desktop and TUI rediscover on every agent build while nothing is connected, the gateway once per cron job), four requests each time. One user hit about 200 failed refreshes a minute and got his IP rate-limited out of the Nous Portal. After: the parked server stays quiet until hermes mcp login or a Desktop re-auth rewrites its token files, then comes back on the next session. The 5-minute self-probe still retries, and three fixes for that slower drip are still in review.

7️⃣ Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini thinking settings that stick

Before: Argon was not in the model lists, any reasoning effort left it at its medium default, and output past 32,768 tokens was cut and reported as a normal stop. On Gemini 3.x, turning reasoning off sent a budget of 0 that those models reject or ignore. After: gemini-4-argon is selectable on Gemini, Vertex, OpenRouter and Nous (Gemini 3.8 Flash stays the default), and effort maps to Google's thinkingLevel by version number for every Gemini 3 and up. On the native endpoints, xhigh and max turn on long decode, up to 262,144 and 1,048,576 output tokens, with a hop ceiling so a server cannot keep billing, and a dropped stream resumes from its last checkpoint instead of starting over. Gaps: no long decode on OpenRouter, proxies or the OAuth Vertex provider, and after a resume the tokens generated before the drop are missing from reported usage. Introductory price: $2 in, $10 out per million tokens, doubling on 1 Dec per Google.

8️⃣ Typing answers the question card

Before: in Desktop, typing in the composer while a clarify card waited cancelled the card with every question unanswered and sent your words as a separate steer, so the model did not know which question they answered. After: the words answer the card's first open question, text that matches a choice label picks that choice, and each Enter answers one question. Slash commands, attachments and an empty Enter (Stop) work as before. The onboarding cards, theme pickers and the connector directory take typed words the same way; the CLI, TUI and messaging apps are unchanged.

9️⃣ MCP tool schemas: reloads and $refs that work

Before: /reload-mcp said reloaded, but a tool that kept its name also kept its old description and parameters. And values behind a $ref in an MCP tool's schema, common with pydantic and zod servers, reached the tool as the model typed them: 5 as a string for an integer field, first_name where the server named the key first name. After: an explicit reload publishes same-name schema changes (the automatic refresh between turns still does not, to protect the prompt cache), and local $refs are followed for type conversion and key mapping. Still not parsed: a JSON string sent for a union with no top-level type.

🔟 29 new plugins in the catalog

Keeping an eye on the agent is the day's theme: two ledgers, an independent verifier, runtime guardrails and a fleet operations page. BrowserPaw, delisted on 3 Oct, is back with credential-free MCP delegation. Catalog entries do not wait for a release: they go live once the published catalog refreshes.

• Oversight and observability: agent-ledger, context-audit, hermes-call-ledger, hermes-guide, hermes-verifier, llm-antidote, operations
• Memory and context: betterdb, hermes-vcc, kumiho-memory, long-conversations, wicked-memory
• Workflows and automation: auto-pin, heartbeat2, myswarm
• Data and search: colorado-traffic, event-read, index-search
• Shopping and ads: adwhispr, channel3
• Languages: hermes-lang-ca, hermes-lang-el, hermes-lang-th
• Phones and apps: hermes-mobile, phone-harness
• Models and accounts: account-pool, netmind-provider
• Messaging and voice: telegram-stickers, ttsbuddy

━━━━━━━━━━

⚙️ Meanwhile, in the engine room

Dozens of fixes landed yesterday that you will probably never see. Most of them went into polishing the new Desktop onboarding before the release cut.

• Telemetry that stopped sending after an update dropped a value old rows still held, like a v0.21.6 Spotify row, now re-buckets or skips that row and sends the rest of the day
• On Linux, a git exiting anywhere on the machine during the launch-time index.lock check no longer fails the Hermes launch
• Windows Store and App Installer updates get past Could not register automatic relaunch, which aborted them before installing
• hermes://plugin/install catalog links, broken since they shipped, now ask the backend for the entry

If you noticed none of this, it worked.

All on main and already shipped. Latest stable: v0.22.0.

Which one hits you most? 👇

Is ChatGPT broken?

@OpenAI, I'm on your $200 Pro plan, which used to be the top tier.
@xai @grok @AnthropicAI, engineers, read this too.

On Sep 29, OpenAI added a $500 tier. Same day, it told $200 subscribers their agent and Codex usage drops from 20x to 10x the Plus allowance starting Oct 30. Pro chat messages go from 200 to 100 a week. Half the usage, same price.

$500 is 2.5x the old top tier, and the old top tier now gets half.

What exactly does that gain anyone?

Over the past months, agent work on my plan got worse: tasks dropped halfway, "done" reports on work that wasn't done, the same steps redone. Dots that used to connect stopped connecting. I emailed OpenAI with the evidence. No real response.

Now the fix is a pricier tier.

Upgrade, or extortion? Hand people a weaker model, then charge more to get the agentic work back?

I won't take that risk. I'm passing on a company that monetizes its own regression.

Credit where it's due: @AnthropicAI has earned it. Claude Opus 5.5 is what agentic work should look like. It holds the task, finishes the job, and they cut its cost instead of raising it.

What I run instead:
- Claude for the agent work that has to be right
- Grok for hands-off agent runs
- Local models on my own hardware: GLM 5.3, a 27B and a 24B uncensored model, Hermes
- No subscription can quietly cut those local ones in half

My charts say the same thing. Google search interest in ChatGPT is down about 15% from its Sep 2025 peak, and a Google TimesFM forecast projects a further dip over the next 26 weeks. If you're putting money into ChatGPT, step down a tier until they fix the problem.

What about Muse? Meta's new model, released Oct 12. Not free. The stronger version (Muse Wonder Full) only runs inside Meta's Muse Code subscription at $50 or $200/month. Regular Muse costs about the same per use as Opus 5.5.
Independent overall score (Artificial Analysis): Opus 5.5 58, Muse Full 56, ChatGPT's top model 53, Grok 4.6 44.
Muse wins at very long coding jobs and context memory, but those are Meta's own tests. Opus beats it at terminal work, computer use, and writing programs from scratch.
I haven't dipped a toe in. I get most things done without adding to my stack.

Check your own numbers (don't ask the chatbot, it can't see your meter and will guess):
- Everyday users: open your account's settings or usage page and screenshot your plan and weekly limits.
- Codex users: type /status and screenshot what it shows.
- Developers: log the x-ratelimit headers your API calls return.

Developers and everyday users alike, drop your plan and numbers below, before and after Oct 30. I'll crunch the consensus and post it, so the regression is on the record, not just a feeling.

Questions:
1. Are you on the new $500 tier? Is there a real difference?
2. Has agent or Codex work gotten worse for you, or is it just me?
3. Who's running local models for real work, and which ones?
4. @OpenAI, will you publish the actual before-and-after limits?
5. @xai, what's your answer for people who need agents that finish the job?
6. Does anybody use Muse? What do you think of it?

Sources: OpenAI Help Center "About ChatGPT Pro tiers"; OpenAI subscriber email as reported by Engadget; Anthropic's Opus 5.5 announcement; Artificial Analysis Muse Wonder review. Chart: Google Trends, forecast TimesFM 2.5, statistical projection, not fact.

The day's later coverage added 3 more Schulz_Research items. The H2 guide math post (17:00 UTC): ASML needs 24.9 to 26.9 billion euros of sales in the second half to hit its own 2026 guide of 43 to 45 billion euros; the first half was 18.1 billion euros; Q3, reporting Wednesday, is guided at 11.0 to 12.0 billion euros; at the midpoints that leaves about 14.4 billion euros for Q4, roughly 55% above the 9.3 billion euros ASML reported in Q2. The silicon photonics DUV post (18:00 UTC): the photonic chips going into co packaged optics are made on 45nm to 180nm processes, none of that needs EUV, so the lithography under the AI optics buildout is ASML's DUV line, and ASML says dry DUV shipments increased markedly this year. Its chart analysis records DUV systems sold by type for 2023 to Q2 2026 (ArF immersion 125, 129, 131, then 23 in Q2 2026; ArF dry 32, 28, 16, then 8; KrF 184, 152, 78, then 35; i line 55, 65, 54, then 9), and ASML's July comments as recorded: dry DUV shipments increased markedly this year (CFO, Q2 2026 call), immersion DUV about 130 shipments expected this year, non EUV net system sales expected to grow around 25% this year, and 75 of 91 lithography systems sold in Q2 2026 were DUV. The platform chart records: GlobalFoundries GF Fotonix (45SPCLO), 45nm SOI 300mm, monolithic photonics and CMOS on one die; TSMC COUPE photonic die, N65 reported, stacked on an electronic die reported at N7 via SoIC; Tower PH18, 180nm reported, adding 300mm silicon photonics capacity in Japan, ready Q4 2027 (Tower 6 K, July 14, 2026); UMC Singapore 12 inch fab, node not disclosed, first mass produced silicon photonics wafers delivered (reported). JSCC2020Lee commented that DUV scanners printing the 45 to 65nm silicon photonics dies for CPO while EUV handles the leading edge logic is the tool mix split that registered. The Tower PH18 Japan capacity line in this chart connects directly back to the morning's Semtech and Tower SiGe capacity deal in Section 5.4: the same company's silicon photonics capacity expansion appears in both the deal reporting and the analyst platform map. (3/5)

4.2 LASERTEC: THE EUV MASK ITEM AND THE MATRICS DUV LINE

Source account: Schulz_Research, posts at 19:00 and 20:00 UTC.

The mask post (19:00 UTC): ASML and TSMC want EUV masks twice as long by 2031, and every one of them will need inspecting; Lasertec (6920 JT), the only commercial seller of actinic EUV mask inspection the author found, just booked 237.5 billion yen of orders, up 126%, and guides 300 to 400 billion yen this fiscal year. The chart analysis records the order history: FY2022 323.7 billion yen, FY2023 186.5 billion yen, FY2024 272.7 billion yen, FY2025 105.2 billion yen, FY2026 237.5 billion yen (+126%), FY2027 estimate guide 300 to 400 billion yen; order backlog 322.9 billion yen at June 30, 2026; ACTIS (actinic EUV) orders 62.0 billion yen in FY2026, from about 10.5 billion yen in FY2025. August comments from CEO Sendoda as recorded: if the material ends up metal related, only ACTIS can penetrate the pellicle and only ACTIS can do the inspection (a tailwind); pellicles are not yet commercialized and pellicle driven orders are so limited so far; A300 released for high NA, with orders expected to emerge from leading edge fabs doing R and D for high NA adoption; orders recovered as production capacity for leading edge nodes (2nm and 3nm equivalent) expanded. Source: Lasertec FY2026 presentation, earnings call transcript and FAQ, August 2026.

The 12 inch mask chart records: a 23% to 50% scanner productivity gain from 6 by 12 inch masks, per an Intel slide at SPIE 2025; 2x mask length, with every inspection stage and handler required to take the new size; 0 mask or inspection suppliers named in the September 8 TSMC and ASML statement. Timeline as recorded: today, High NA prints 26 by 16.5 mm per shot on a 6 inch mask, half the standard 26 by 33 mm field, with large AI dies stitched from 2 exposures; 2026, Lasertec guides FY2027 orders of 300 to 400 billion yen on 2nm, 3nm and 1.4nm node work, with no mention of 12 inch masks in its August materials; 2027, ASML High NA to start supporting high volume manufacturing; 2028, Samsung High NA in DRAM volume production; 2030, TSMC High NA volume production, still on 6 inch masks; 2031, 12 inch EUV mask pilot production line (TSMC and ASML); 2033, the lithography ecosystem ready for volume manufacturing on 12 inch masks.

The MATRICS post (20:00 UTC): Lasertec sells 2 kinds of mask inspection, and China can only buy one of them; its CEO said in August that Chinese inquiries for the DUV light line, MATRICS, are very strong, and that MATRICS as a whole may come close to doubling, with China's share holding steady. This is the export control hinge of the test section: the actinic EUV line (ACTIS) is the line China cannot buy, and the DUV line (MATRICS) is the line where Chinese inquiry strength is itself the data point. Both Lasertec items trace to one author's reporting of Lasertec's own August materials; the order and backlog figures are attributed on the charts to company documents, and the ledger files them as single reporter, company sourced.

4.3 TERADYNE ULTRAFLEXPLUS S AND THE BOOTH PROGRAM

Source account: Teradyneinc, post at 01:01 UTC October 14 (06:01 PM PT October 13), the day's only dedicated test equipment vendor item in the evening roundup.

Post text: Day 1 at SEMICON West; listen from our experts on how test and automation work side by side at booth 1143, with UltraFLEXplus S and a Universal Robots cobot; stop by the booth and join our 15 minute talks tomorrow. The video preview still analysis records: 2 men in conference badges in front of a Teradyne test system with a green board and a Universal Robots cobot arm behind them; the man on the right wears a Universal Robots jacket with a badge reading Mike DeGrace; booth signage partly reads Innovative Test Solutions for Leading Edge Technologies, with an aisle 1200 hanging sign above; no specs or figures. The item is a booth presence record, not a product launch record: the archive contains no UltraFLEXplus S specifications, no pricing and no customer names, and the ledger files it accordingly. Its analytical value is positional: test, represented in the analyst work by the Schulz_Research series as the gating step for both yield and throughput, was represented on the floor by a test plus automation pairing (tester plus cobot), which matches the Smart Manufacturing Pavilion's robotics theme in Section 6.

4.4 KULICKE AND SOFFA AND THE SEMI AWARD

Source account: SEMIAmericas, post at 19:15 UTC, official program cluster. Full treatment is in Section 6.4; the equipment fact is recorded here: Kulicke and Soffa (KLIC) is the recipient of the 2026 SEMI Award for North America, for Advancements in Thermo Compression Bonding Technology, with the award card citing distinguished leadership and sustained technical advancement in TCB, a field central to the progression of advanced semiconductor packaging and heterogeneous integration. Thermo compression bonding and Applied's hybrid bonding are competing and complementary answers to the same stacking problem, and day 1 gave both of them headline treatment within 3 hours of each other; that juxtaposition is in the archive, and any stronger claim about which bonding route is winning would be interpretation beyond it.

4.5 ENABLING ITEMS: PURE WAFER PSC, THE OIF SKEW SLIDE, AND THE GE AEROSPACE PRINTED ELECTRONICS SLIDE

Pure Wafer (newsfile_corp at 20:51 UTC and PureWafer at 20:59 UTC, 2 accounts reporting the same announcement): Pure Wafer announced a new Precision Surface Cleaning process technology (PSC) for semiconductor manufacturing and quantum sensing, at SEMICON West, with the announcement carried under hashtags including PartsCleaning, SEMI, SemiconductorFabrication, SEMICONWEST and WaferReclaim. No process specifications, no customer names and no performance figures appear in either post; the ledger files the announcement as corroborated as an announcement (2 accounts) and unverified as to any technical content, because none was posted.

The OIF skew slide (insane_analyst, 21:02 UTC, post text: Oh wow this is revolting): the image analysis records OIF slide 39, Frequency Dependent Intra Pair Skew (Copyright 2026 OIF; Figure 5, OIF FD CEI 448G 01.0, Next Generation CEI 448G Framework). The 224G transmission media observations as recorded: PCB traces and twinax cables exhibit distinctly different skew versus frequency profiles; the twinax examples show large, non monotonic skew variation across frequency; intra pair skew can amplify jitter and inter symbol interference and contribute to differential to common mode conversion. The 448G implications as recorded: cable and interconnect designs must control skew across the required bandwidth; the industry needs agreed interpretation, requirements and mitigation methods; fixtures and measurement methods must extend beyond the 67 GHz range used for 224G. The chart plots skew in picoseconds against frequency 0 to 65 GHz for 1 inch and 6 inch PCB traces and 0.5m and 1.0m twinax cables.

The GE Aerospace slide (SEMIAmericas Future Technology Sessions post, 18:22 UTC, photo 3 of 4): Additive (Printed) Electronics; the future of additive manufacturing is 3D printing of functional electronic materials; printed trace specs shown: 50 um trace width, 100 um spacing, 5 to 10 um thick prints; advantages listed: quick prototyping, printed harsh environment use (right edge cropped in the photo), new electronics form factors, flexible device integration, 3D direct write printing; footer GE Aerospace, cleared for public release. Small figures, but they are the only printed electronics specifications in the day's archive, and they came from a slide photo inside an official account's photo set, a good example of the image analysis rule of thumb that substance often sits in the image rather than the post text.

5. GEOPOLITICS, INDUSTRIAL POLICY, AND DELEGATIONS

5.1 THE GEOPOLITICAL SUMMIT

Source account: SEMIAmericas, wrap post at 23:15 UTC; session graphic posted 19:00 UTC.

The wrap post text: the Geopolitical Summit at SEMICON West just wrapped up at Moscone North Hall; featured discussions included a keynote speaker, Brandon Remington from the International Trade Administration, and a fireside chat with Tim Archer of Lam Research and Representative Darrell Issa (post text truncated in the archive, the Congressman's state and party not carried in the post). The session graphic in the earlier SEMIAmericas post records the logistics: Geopolitical Summit, Tuesday, October 13, 2026, 1:30 to 3:30 PM PT, Moscone North Hall, Lower Level, CEO Summit Stage. The 3 wrap photos are stage photos only, per the image analyses: a lone speaker in a blue suit in front of a stylized Washington DC and US Capitol backdrop rendered as a glowing circuit board; 2 men seated in armchairs for the fireside, identified by the post text as Archer and Issa; and a 6 person panel with a woman moderating. No slide text, names or figures are readable in any of the 3 photos.

That absence is itself the finding for this section: the archive establishes who keynoted, who sat for the fireside, when and where the summit ran, and nothing about what either man said. No attendee post in the day's archive quotes Remington or Archer, and no policy announcement, export control change or subsidy figure traces to the summit in the record. Any report that filled that gap from general knowledge would be inventing the day's most sensitive content, so this report records the summit as a delivered program item with verified participants and unverified substance, and puts attendee or press capture of the Remington keynote and the Archer and Issa fireside at the top of the day 2 watch list in Section 9.

5.2 THE ARIZONA DELEGATION

Source account: SandraWatsonAZ, post at 23:21 UTC.

Post text: incredible kick off to SEMICON West, with more than 30 Arizona partners in attendance; honored to join a panel discussion moderated by Ian Steff on the critical infrastructure, workforce and collaborative frameworks needed to support ecosystem wide semiconductor growth. The 4 photos are people and stage photos per the analyses: a group photo of about 20 members of the Arizona delegation in front of a blue and orange Arizona booth backdrop with a state outline graphic; a stage photo of a panel with the moderator at a yellow SEMI lectern and 4 panelists seated; a reception photo; and a lounge entrance photo whose sponsor list at right includes Macquarie, ABM, ACM Research, AG Semiconductor, Exentec and Exyte. The hard content is the count (more than 30 partners) and the panel subject (infrastructure, workforce, collaborative frameworks), both single source from a delegation participant's own post, which is the expected sourcing for a delegation presence item and is filed as such.

5.3 THE MEXICO DELEGATION

Source account: SE_mx (the Mexican economy secretariat's account), post at 23:50 UTC, a formal statement post (Comunicado Economia): Mexico strengthens its presence in the global semiconductor industry during SEMICON West 2026, with a link to the statement. The 2 photos record about 35 members of the Mexican delegation on a red carpet at the Mexico pavilion, with banners for Jalisco and Coahuila visible, a CANIETI banner (Camara Nacional de la Industria de Telecomunicaciones y Tecnologias de la Informacion) and a Mexican flag; and a smaller group of 4 in front of the CANIETI banner. No figures, company names or commitments appear in the post or the photos; the statement itself sits behind the link and was not captured as text in the archive. Filed as an official presence record, single source, with the linked statement's contents unverified within the archive.

5.4 THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC DELEGATION, AND THE SEMTECH AND TOWER DEAL IN ITS INDUSTRIAL POLICY FRAME

Source accounts: LosMocanos (18:31 UTC), ElDia_do (19:26 UTC), SanzLovaton (19:46 UTC and 23:45 UTC).

LosMocanos and ElDia_do both carried the same headline, in Spanish: a Dominican delegation met with more than 20 US companies at SEMICON West; the ElDia_do post attributes the report to Dilenni Bonilla and links the El Dia story. SanzLovaton's own post said, in Spanish, that the Dominican Republic has much to offer the semiconductor industry, presenting the country at SEMICON West 2026 in San Francisco and showing its talent and industrial experience; the video preview still shows the minister speaking to camera in a conference hall under a CEO Summit banner, wearing a Dominican Republic flag pin. His later post supplied the opening keynote photos used in Section 6.3. The more than 20 companies figure is corroborated by 2 outlets carrying the same report, which is corroboration of the report, not independent verification of the meetings; no company is named in either post.

The industrial policy frame for the day's first headline item belongs here as well as in the equipment sections, because the deal is a capacity geography story. SingularityRes, post at 13:29 UTC, the day's first headline item: Semtech locks dedicated SiGe capacity at Tower, US, Israel, Japan. Post text: expanded multi year deal, Semtech investing in dedicated SiGe capacity at Tower fabs in the US, Israel and Japan (Tower and Semtech press release, October 13); for AI data center optical and copper interconnects, TIAs (post text truncated in the archive at the product list). The post carried 3 photo media items; the media rows in the archive carry no stored analysis for them, so no slide figures can be quoted for this item, and the report does not invent any. The delivery note records the same facts: dedicated SiGe capacity at Tower across the US, Israel and Japan, multi year, for AI data center optical and copper interconnects.

Why it led the day, stated as interpretation grounded in the archive's own later material: SiGe capacity for transimpedance amplifiers and related interconnect parts sits directly upstream of the optical buildout argued about all afternoon in Sections 6 and 7, the deal spreads that capacity across 3 allied geographies rather than concentrating it, and Tower appears 2 more times in the day's record (the PH18 180nm silicon photonics capacity in Japan, ready Q4 2027, in the Schulz_Research platform chart, and the general fab expansion chorus). A dedicated capacity investment, as opposed to a purchase order, is also the same commitment pattern as the NVIDIA prepayment to KYEC recorded in the Nodus42 filings graphic: buyers paying to reserve scarce upstream capacity. That pattern, capacity reservation as the day's recurring transaction form, is one of the few genuinely cross cutting findings of day 1, and it is interpretation built entirely from archive items named here.

5.5 CXMT READ THROUGHS AS INDUSTRIAL POLICY (CROSS REFERENCE)

The CXMT cluster is treated in full in Section 3.4. Its industrial policy content is recorded here for the section's completeness: the cluster's technical argument is inseparable from an export control fact that multiple archive contributors state in their own words, namely that EUV is not available to CXMT (Schulz_Research), that HBM is a story of stacking, TSVs and export controls (sem2investor), and that Lasertec's actinic EUV inspection line is the line China cannot buy while its DUV MATRICS line draws very strong Chinese inquiries (Schulz_Research, Section 4.2). Taken together, and labeled as interpretation, day 1's archive describes a 2 tier equipment world from 3 independent directions at once: a leading edge tier where EUV, actinic inspection and hybrid bonding compound, and a DUV tier where ingenuity (4F2 cell geometry, MATRICS inspection, multi patterning) extracts density at rising cost per bit. The Geopolitical Summit ran on the same afternoon as that description was being assembled by the analyst community, even though the archive holds no words from the summit itself.

6. SMART MANUFACTURING, MEDTECH, AND THE OFFICIAL PROGRAM

6.1 DAY 1 WELCOME AND THE SHAPE OF THE SHOW

Source accounts: SEMIAmericas (welcome post, 14:00 UTC; Lam Research speaker lineup post, 16:00 UTC), TTradDashboard and ttvresearch (AMAT notices, covered in Section 2.1).

SEMIAmericas welcome post text: Welcome to Day 1 of SEMICON West 2026 in San Francisco. Highlights today: CEO Summit Keynotes and Geopolitical Summit; Smart Manufacturing plus Smart MedTech; APHI Summit; Workforce Development Pavilion; Sustainability Pavilion; SEMICON WestFest; and so much more. The Lam Research post records that Lam is the SEMICON West 2026 Platinum Sponsor and promotes its speaker lineup, with a marketing graphic of the SABRE 3D tool that the image analysis records as carrying no specs, numbers or product data. These 2 posts, with the Intel Foundry Platinum Sponsor post in the afternoon coverage (Intel Foundry supporting SEMICON West 2026 as a Platinum Sponsor, Tuesday to Thursday, October 13 to 15, Moscone Center, with a generic sponsor graphic and no product content), establish the sponsor and program skeleton the rest of the official coverage hangs on.

6.2 SMART MANUFACTURING PAVILION AND THE DAY 2 SESSIONS

Source account: SEMIAmericas, post at 23:46 UTC.

Post text: the Smart Manufacturing Pavilion has been action packed, and we are just getting started; join us at the Moscone North Hall Expo Floor to check out tomorrow's sessions, including Agentic AI and LLMs in Manufacturing Operation number 2, and Physical AI in the Fab: Robotics, Simulation, and (post text truncated in the archive). The 3 photos are crowd and booth photos per the analyses: a packed pavilion session audience with aisle markers 5100 and 5200 and an INFICON booth sign; Rockwell Automation and Lavorro booths with attendees networking; and Seeq, MOXA and Spotfire stands with a Costa Rica pavilion sign in the background, aisle markers 5400 and 5500. No slide content was readable in any pavilion photo, so the archive's Smart Manufacturing content for day 1 is the session titles for day 2 and the pavilion's vendor presence, nothing more. The day 2 titles matter for Section 9: Agentic AI and LLMs in Manufacturing Operation number 2 is the smart manufacturing counterpart of the agentic pod thesis in Section 3.1, the same word, agentic, doing work at both the wafer demand layer and the fab operations layer on consecutive days.

6.3 OPENING KEYNOTES: STOCKUNAS AND MANOCHA, THE $1 TRILLION TOAST, AND THE CEO SUMMIT

Source accounts: SanzLovaton (keynote photos, 23:45 UTC), SEMIAmericas (opening post, 19:00 UTC), TokyoElectronUS (keynote promo, 19:00 UTC), BenBajarin (Dickerson quote, 16:26 UTC).

SanzLovaton's post, in Spanish, records that the day began with the talks by Joe Stockunas, president of SEMI Americas, and Ajit Manocha, president and CEO of SEMI (the post uses the SEMIconex handle for SEMI), during the opening of the event in San Francisco. Its photos record: the minister in conversation at a reception; a keynote stage whose screen reads Industry Highlights and Outlook to 2035, Ajit Manocha, SEMI President and CEO, with the SEMI logo and a Golden Gate Bridge backdrop; the Moscone Center exterior with the SEMICON West October 13 to 15 banner; and a reception photo with the minister's badge readable as Eduardo Sanz Lovaton. No figures from Manocha's outlook to 2035 were captured in any photo, a notable gap given that the same author's delegation supplied the archive's only images of the session; the outlook's title and horizon year (2035) are all the archive holds.

SEMIAmericas' opening post records: SEMICON West has officially started; the morning began with a champagne toast to celebrate $1 trillion in industry revenue; the CEO Summit featured an inspiring keynote from Lalitha Immaneni of Intel Foundry, and special appearances by Mayor Daniel Lurie of San Francisco (post text truncated). The toast photo's screen reads, per the image analysis: The semiconductor industry has reached $1 trillion in revenue, 4 years ahead of projections, over a Golden Gate Bridge backdrop, with the audience raising glasses. The $1 trillion figure and the 4 years ahead claim are the official show's own framing, single source (the organizer's account and its stage screen), and they sit in deliberate contrast with the afternoon's selloff color: the industry celebrating a milestone 4 years early on the morning its largest equipment vendor fell 6.69% for not sizing the next milestone. That contrast is in the record; calling it irony is interpretation, and it is labeled as such.

TokyoElectronUS posted that TEL COO Jack Ishida takes the CEO Summit stage for a keynote, Powering Sustainable Growth in the AI Era, with the promo graphic recording Thursday, October 15, 10:05 AM PST, Moscone Center North Hall, Lower Level, CEO Summit Stage. This is a day 3 item announced on day 1, and it is carried into Section 9. BenBajarin's program note records the day's most quoted sentence, from AMAT CEO Gary Dickerson: I believe we manufacture miracles all the time, with BenBajarin adding that manufacturing semis is indeed a modern miracle. No data, and none needed; it is the tone marker for the breakfast.

6.4 THE SEMI AWARD, FUTURE TECHNOLOGY SESSIONS, AND THE REMAINING PROGRAM CLUSTER

The Kulicke and Soffa award (SEMIAmericas, 19:15 UTC) is recorded in Section 4.4; the award card image adds the citation language: K and S is formally recognized for distinguished leadership and sustained technical advancement in Thermo Compression Bonding (TCB), a field central to the progression of advanced semiconductor packaging and heterogeneous integration, and a second photo shows the stage presentation with recipients beside a large gold star trophy graphic under the event banner (Oct 13 to 15, 2026, Moscone Center, Transform Tomorrow).

Future Technology Sessions (SEMIAmericas, 18:22 UTC): the post invites attendees to the sessions on emerging technologies and new possibilities; of its 4 photos, 1 is the title card, 1 a speaker at a podium with no slide visible, 1 the GE Aerospace additive printed electronics slide recorded in Section 4.5, and 1 an audience photo. The sessions post at 19:30 UTC (SEMIAmericas) carries a photo collage whose partially visible slide concerns time series anomaly analysis (labeled features, GRU, semi supervised data, K means clustering, flagging or clustering anomalous patterns, with state definitions Operational, Saturating and Breakthrough); no session title is readable, and no figures were recorded from it. That partial slide is the archive's only smart manufacturing technical content for day 1, and its fragmentary state is recorded rather than reconstructed.

🔹散户投资者净卖出 SK 海力士（0.88 亿美元），同时净买入三星电子（0.77 亿美元）。

🔹浦项 FM (003670) 上涨 4.6%，三星 SDI (006400) 上涨 5.5%，SK INNO (096770) 上涨 4.1%，L&F (066970) 上涨 6.5%，LS MAT (417200) 上涨 6.8%。
🔹第一，市场持续乐观认为，在欧中达成限制中国混动汽车出口协议背景下，韩国电池厂商有望重新夺回欧洲市场份额。

🔹汽车板块｜美国 9 月汽车价格更新：凯利蓝皮书于当地时间 10 月 13 日发布 9 月价格数据，行业车辆优惠后净售价同比上涨 1.4%，达到 47202 美元。
🔹现代 + 起亚（HMK）车辆净售价 35028 美元，同比上涨 1.0%，环比上涨 0.5%。
🔹凭借优于行业的定价水平，叠加偏向混动车型的强大产品矩阵，我们持续预期现代和起亚在美国市场的份额将继续提升。

❓WHAT DROVE MARKETS? 什么推动了市场？

🌏亚洲股市收盘涨跌互现，投资者在美国 CPI 数据公布前保持谨慎，而 ASML 的财报及供应前景评论在午盘交易中拖累了地区半导体情绪。
📉中国和韩国因科技板块再度走弱表现落后，香港和日本在 ASML 引发的逆转后回吐早前涨幅，而台湾在台积电财报公布前收高。
🛡️能源、公用事业及部分大宗商品相关个股等防御性板块在全区范围内普遍跑赢于大盘，而中国市场成交额依然低迷，投资者总体上采取避险立场。

🗺️REGIONAL WRAPS 区域综述
🇦🇺澳大利亚：AS51 指数下跌 0.64%。
📝澳大利亚股市收低，金融板块领跌，因美国银行财报表现不一带来负面传导。
📝CBA 下跌 2.2%，Bendigo & Adelaide Bank 下跌 3.5%，而能源板块表现优异，上涨 2.1%，因油价高企支撑 Karoon Energy 上涨 6.5%。
📝科技和通信服务板块均上涨 0.5%，材料板块下跌 1.0%。
📝Austal 大涨 10.5%，此前该公司延长了韩华对其美国子公司的收购尽职调查期，而 Superloop 在券商首次给予买入评级后上涨 5.7%。
📝Paladin Energy 下跌 9.1%，因铀矿股走弱，而 Orora 下跌 5.5%，此前公司指引 2027 财年集团息税前利润将下降。
📝嘉能可完成 ASX 上市首秀，收于 11.23 澳元，成交股票价值超过 13 亿澳元。
📝澳元 / 美元报约 0.6931，利率基本持平，而西太平洋 - 墨尔本研究所领先指标 9 月环比下降 0.06%，显示增长动能持续低于趋势水平。
🇹🇼台湾：TWSE 指数上涨 0.59%。
📝台湾股市在台积电财报公布前反弹。台积电（2330）开盘走势强劲，但遭遇卖压，股价回落至平盘附近，其他大型股则表现平淡，尤其是联发科（2454），在持续表现不佳的情况下下跌 1.1%。
📝长期科技主题出现技术性反弹，由存储和 MLCC 个股领涨，同时 CPO 板块也因美国 OCP 峰会而走高。
📝非科技板块表现不一，但石化板块大涨 9.3%，仍为表现最佳板块，多只个股涨停。
📝随着投资者在台积电业绩公布前观望，交易活动转淡，市场成交额环比下降 23%。
🇰🇷韩国：KOSPI 指数下跌 0.44%。
📝韩国股市最初从前一交易日的低点反弹，但随着 ASML 发布财报后半导体股大幅下挫，涨幅逐渐收窄。
📝国内机构是主要的支撑力量，集中买入科技股，而外资和散户投资者全天均为净卖出。
📝SK 海力士 (000660) 下跌 1.7%，三星电子 (005930) 在双双高开后收平，而半导体设备股包括 JUSUNG ENG（036930）和 EUGENE TECH（084370）则大幅下跌。
📝电动汽车供应链股表现优于大盘，受 ESS 市场增长及欧中协议持续乐观情绪的提振。
🇯🇵日本：日经 225 指数下跌 0.05%。
📝日本股市收盘涨跌互现，日经 225 微跌 0.05%，东证指数下跌 0.3%，此前尾盘半导体板块遭抛售，抹去了早盘涨幅。
📝两大指数在盘中大部分时间均处于上涨区间，直至阿斯麦发布财报及供应前景评论，引发芯片相关个股再度走弱。
📝能源、材料和公用事业板块表现领先，金融、医疗保健和房地产板块表现落后。
📝奥林巴斯（7733）因收到美国食品药品监督管理局的新警告而暴跌 13.5%，金融板块整体表现不佳。
📝企业活动保持活跃，Ichigo（2337）和大东药品（4577）宣布股票回购，日本航空（9201）则下单订购 26 架巴西航空工业 E190-E2 飞机。
📝日本 5 年期国债拍卖需求稳健，日元在美国消费者价格指数发布前变动不大。
🇨🇳中国：沪深 300 指数下跌 1.36%。
📝午后交易再度走弱，带动中国股市下行，成交额收于 1.43 万亿元人民币以下，回落至国庆假期前录得的年内低点附近。
📝科技硬件板块尾盘走势趋弱，创业板权重股在短暂反弹一日后再度下跌约 6%。
📝估值同样持续承压，中际旭创前瞻市盈率跌至 2025 年 5 月以来最低水平。
📝防御板块表现领先，石油、公用事业和煤炭是市场中为数不多的亮点。
📝宏观方面，出口和进口均大幅超出市场预期，同比分别增长 36.3% 和 31.0%。
📝中国 9 月贸易顺差从 8 月的 1191 亿美元扩大至 1335 亿美元，创下有记录以来最大单月顺差。
📝在美国 CPI 数据公布前，投资者保持谨慎。
🇭🇰香港：恒生指数下跌 0.13%。
📝香港股市收盘涨跌互现，恒生指数微跌 0.1%，而恒生科技指数上涨 0.9%，受中国互联网股在双十一前空头回补反弹的支撑。
📝恒生指数早盘一度走高，但午后因阿斯麦财报发布，科技和半导体板块再度遭到抛售而转跌。
📝通信服务、能源、必需消费品板块表现领先，医疗保健、房地产、金融和材料板块则表现落后。
📝美团（3690）大涨 6.6%，小米（1810）上涨 5.4%，创科实业（0669）上涨 3.7%。
📝下跌标的方面，信达生物（1801）、中国生物制药（1177）、路劲集团（0960）、宁德时代（3100）、广汽集团（0005）拖累市场情绪。
📝南向资金持续疲软，内地投资者连续第二个交易日净卖出。
🇮🇩东盟：JCI 指数上涨 0.38%。
📝印尼股市从周二创下的 7 月低点收盘水平反弹，必需消费品、公用事业、材料和房地产板块领涨，公用事业是唯一收跌的板块。
📝印尼盾小幅走强，10 年期政府债券收益率基本持平于 7.20%，而外国投资者在 10 月 13 日录得净买入债券 2840 万美元。
📝SET 指数下跌 0.16%。泰国股市基本持平；通信服务、能源和公用事业板块表现领先，而房地产和医疗保健板块表现落后。
📝PTTEP 在成交量放大下上涨 3.3%。
📝泰国将 2026 年 GDP 增长预测从 1.5% 上调至 2.1%，提供了温和的宏观支撑背景。
🇮🇳印度：NIFTY 指数下跌 0.56%。
📝印度市场开盘走高，IT 股持续上涨，抵消了金融股下跌与油价上行带来的拖累。
📝然而，该指数随后走势逆转，跌破 22600 关口，创下盘中新低，当日下跌 0.5%。卢比依然坚挺，上涨 30 个基点至 95。
📝板块方面，能源、IT 和快速消费品板块领涨，制药、金融和房地产板块跌幅最大；IT 板块仍为正面。
📝在个股层面，市场情绪喜忧参半，印度市场整体仍处于 4:3 的多空局面。

$ASML  2026 Q3 财报深度拆解：业绩与毛利创历史新高，为何股价反而下挫？

光刻机巨头 ASML（阿斯麦）刚发布了 2026 财年第三季度财报。尽管营收与利润均创下历史新高，且 EPS 大超预期，但由于市场先前期待过高以及未来产能扩张面临极限，公司股价在盘后走低。

以下是核心要点梳理👇

📊 1. 核心财务数据（创历史新高）

每股收益 (EPS)：$14.65（预期 $12.13），大幅超预期 20.77%。
净销售额 (Net Sales)：117 亿欧元（约 132.1 亿美元），达指引上限，超预期 0.38%。
净利润 (Net Income)：50 亿欧元（含 Mistral 第一期投资重估收益 5 亿欧元）。
毛利率 (Gross Margin)：达 57.5%（创历史新高），远超预期。
装机基地业务 (Installed Base)：营收 33 亿欧元（超指引 4 亿欧元），同比大增约 50%。

🔮 2. 上调全年前景与 Q4 指引

2026 全年营收：上调至 440亿~450亿欧元（同比增长约 36%）。
2026 全年毛利率：上调至约 56%（年初指引仅为 51%~53%）。
全业务增长分布：EUV 业务年增 >45%，非 EUV 业务增 ~20%，中国市场业务占比约 20%。
2026 Q4 指引：预计营收 142亿~152亿欧元，毛利率约 57%。

🏭 3. 产能紧张与需求爆发（重点）

需求可见度延伸至 2028+：
CEO Christophe Fouquet 表示，客户短期需求增加且持续延长，普遍预计供不应求将至少持续至 2028 年，部分订单已排至 2029/2030 年。

扩产计划面临瓶颈：
原定计划在 2027 年和 2028 年分别扩产 30%，但管理层坦言这仍无法满足客户需求，正积极寻找 2028 年及以后的额外扩产方案。

出货量拉升：2026 年计划交付约 65 台 EUV 系统（同比大增 >50%）。

💡 4. 技术与产品里程碑

High NA EUV 进展：
台积电 (TSMC)：联合成立 12 英寸掩模版 (reticle) 财团，并确认将于 2030 年左右 将 High NA 导入量产。
三星 (Samsung)：宣布将于 2028 年 开始将 High NA 投入量产。
英特尔 (Intel)：继续在大规模量产中运行该系统并增加晶圆层数。

新一代设备生产力提升：
NXE:3800F：产能将从 230 wph（片/小时）提升至 260 wph，2027年小批量推出。
YieldStar 550（计量测试设备）：生产力大幅提升 60%，专为 14 埃米（14A）Logic 和 1d DRAM 节点设计。

📉 5. 为什么业绩亮眼股价反而下跌？

营收超预期幅度较小：EPS 虽然大超，但营收仅超 0.38%，显示未来的增长空间或已被市场充分预估。

估值处于高位：目前 P/E 达 55.23，接近 52 周高点区间，资金在利好出尽后倾向获利了结。

产能限制限制短期上限：尽管订单爆棚，但产能无法立刻再翻倍，短期内难以提供更具爆发性的业绩指引。

Gemini 4 Argon is now GA via the Gemini API (model ID: gemini-4-argon). Key details for engineers building agentic systems:

Pricing
- $2 / 1M input, $10 / 1M output (introductory, through Nov 30), then $4 / $20
- Cached input billed at 95% off

Why caching matters for agents
- Every loop iteration re-sends the full context: system prompt, tool schemas, prior turns
- 20 steps x 30K-token context = 600K input tokens: ~$1.20 uncached vs ~$0.06 at full cache hits
- Design implication: keep the static prefix (instructions, tool definitions) identical across steps and append dynamic state at the end

Context and decoding
- 1M-token limit unified across input and output (previous output cap: 64K)
- Long decodes run through a new continuation protocol

Agent safety
- 0.7% attack success on Gray Swan's indirect prompt injection benchmark (15 adaptive attempts)
- Shortcut attempts on coding tasks reduced to 2%
- Trained to pause for human confirmation before irreversible actions

Reported results
- #1 on Vals Index, 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1
- Optimized Google's ADK overnight: -40% session prep time in long sessions, -21% cold import time
- 2.85x vLLM speedup on Gemma 4 E2B (A100): ~37.9K to 108K+ tokens/s with full token parity

先進封裝成AI晶片新戰場：效能不再只看製程
AI晶片要繼續變強，瓶頸愈來愈不只在電晶體能縮多小，也在運算晶片與HBM能否被高密度整合。當最先進製程成本與難度同步上升，先進封裝已從後段工序變成效能、產能與供應鏈競爭的關鍵。

過去業界主要靠縮小電晶體、提高單一晶片密度來推進效能與能源效率；但進入奈米尺度後，製程推進更困難、代價也更高。超微與英特爾在AI熱潮前，便已將大型CPU拆分為多塊晶片，再透過封裝整合。部分晶片可使用較成熟的製程，除了控制成本，也有助於改善良率。

AI需求讓這條路線更受矚目。輝達的AI晶片仰賴台積電的先進封裝，在同一封裝內結合AI運算晶片與大量高頻寬記憶體（HBM）。封裝產能一度限制輝達的銷售成長；台積電近年將舊晶圓廠轉為封裝設施，並把相關產能擴增數倍。台積電將於周四公布季度財報，封裝布局與客戶協作進展將是市場關注焦點之一。

下一步不只是把晶片並排相連，而是朝上下立體堆疊發展。這也改變了封裝的產業定位：原本毛利較低、創新較少的環節，正被晶圓代工廠納入更核心的技術與製造能力。應用材料執行長Gary Dickerson於8月表示，該公司今年封裝相關營收預計成長逾70%。

一項值得留意的解讀是，AI晶片競爭未必只由最先進製程決定；能否把不同晶片、記憶體與產能有效整合，可能同樣左右產品推出速度與供應能力。

【今日市場重點｜2026-10-13】

今日主線：AI一方面支撐全球增長、企業投資及銀行業務，另一方面亦透過債券、交叉投資及未來採購承諾，逐步形成互相連接嘅金融風險。

美國大型銀行未顯示信貸急凍，但融資成本上升、資本市場活動放慢同信貸撥備增加，已開始進入實際業績。

【IMF世界經濟展望｜屬預測，並非實際增長】

IMF最新預測：

• 全球實質增長：2026年3.1%，較7月上調0.1個百分點
• 全球實質增長：2027年3.4%，維持7月預測
• 美國：2026及2027年均為2.3%
• 中國：2026年4.5%、2027年4.0%，兩年均較7月下調0.1個百分點
• 全球通脹：2026年4.7%、2027年4.1%
【能源情景】
IMF基準情景假設霍爾木茲海峽於2027年3月重開、航運到同年10月正常化，並假設平均油價為：
• 2026年：每桶US$96
• 2027年：每桶US$87
如果油價維持每桶US$130至2027年第一季，IMF估計全球增長會分別被削低0.2及0.5個百分點，2027年通脹則可能高1.1個百分點至5.2%。

【AI對增長嘅兩面情景】

IMF估計，較快採用AI可以令2029年全球產出較基準高0.6%。

但下行情景唔係單純假設「AI回報下降」，而係同時包含：
• AI投資下跌
• 股市及相關資產價格回落
• 全球債券收益率上升
• 金融環境收緊

在呢個組合情景下，2028年全球產出可能較基準低1.1%，美國低1.8%；但IMF表示，該情景仍未令全球增長跌至衰退水平。

【IMF金融穩定報告｜AI融資網絡】

IMF壓力測試顯示，資本較弱銀行所佔全球銀行資產比例，由2025年測試嘅18%升至22%。

不過亦要平衡理解：整體銀行資本仍高於最低要求；在壓力情景下，全球銀行平均CET1資本比率下降約150點子至約11.5%。

IMF亦檢視自2023年以來14宗公開AI交易，涉及約：
• US$300bn股權投資
• US$650bn債務
• 約US$1.4tn未來收入、服務或晶片採購承諾
真正風險唔只係總債務，而係投資、借貸及未來採購承諾集中於互相連接嘅企業之間。
如果主要AI企業嘅收入預期或估值下調，壓力可能同時傳到投資者、債權人、供應商及承接長期合約嘅企業。

IMF同時指出，hyperscalers目前已佔全球投資級債券發行約10%，2024年尚不足1%。

【美國銀行業績｜未見信貸急凍，但唔係全面強勁】

JPMorgan：

• 淨利潤US$15.3bn
• 每股盈利US$5.57，低過市場預期約US$5.85
• 剔除US$658m投資證券虧損後，每股盈利US$5.75
• 固定收益交易收入按年跌4%
• 信貸成本US$2.7bn，包括US$2.2bn淨撇帳及US$539m淨撥備增加
• 撇除市場業務後，淨利息收入升6%
• 平均貸款按年升10%

Wells Fargo：

• 淨利息收入升5%至US$12.52bn
• 資產上限解除後，貸款資產負債表重新擴張
Goldman Sachs：
• 淨收入US$18.68bn
• 淨利潤US$5.29bn
• 股票業務收入按年升72%
• 投行費用按年升21%，但按季跌5%

Citigroup：

• 淨利潤按年升40%至US$5.25bn
• 每股盈利US$2.85，高過市場預期US$2.66
• 投行收入按年升9%，但按季跌13%
• 交易收入按年升6%，但按季跌13%
• 信用卡業務利潤按年跌8%，相關信貸撥備升4%

Reuters指出，今季市場波動背景包括聯儲局9月加息及長債收益率急升。

所以較準確嘅判斷係：貸款、交易及企業融資仍然運作，但融資成本上升、資本市場活動放慢及信貸撥備增加，已開始影響銀行業績。

【騰訊發債｜高評級發行人仍能取得資金】

Reuters引述直接知情人士報道，騰訊正籌集至少US$4.5bn等值美元及離岸人民幣債券。
交易文件顯示：
• 認購需求合共約US$17.1bn
• 當中約US$1.4bn屬主承銷商興趣
• 美元10年期債初步價格指引約為美國國債收益率加115點子
• 騰訊評級為Moody’s A1、S&P A+及Fitch A
• 公司上一次發債係今年6月
騰訊2026年上半年資本開支為人民幣963億元，去年同期為459億元。
強勁認購只能證明高評級、現金流充裕嘅發行人仍能取得大額融資；唔代表槓桿較高嘅AI企業、SPV或者依靠未來租賃收入嘅項目，都可以用相若條款融資。
較準確嘅結論係：
資本市場未全面關閉，但發行人之間嘅融資能力、條款及價格差異正在擴大。

【AI CREDIT DASHBOARD｜重大事件更新】

整體維持🟠 Orange：風險上升，但未確認AI資本開支周期斷裂。
今次IMF報告提供咗更具體嘅系統性證據：

• AI債券供應佔投資級市場比例急升
• 股權、債務及未來收入承諾互相連接
• 較弱AI企業嘅估值或收入下調，可能向其他資產負債表傳導

但目前仍未見以下因素同時惡化：
• AI收入及實際需求廣泛倒退
• Backlog／RPO取消或轉化明顯轉弱
• GPU長期低利用率或大規模減值
• 自由現金流缺口失控
• 信用條件全面收緊
• 大型企業被迫削減資本開支
完整Dashboard維持星期五集中更新；今日只記錄IMF報告呢項重大風險事件。
【今日判斷】

今日最重要嘅矛盾係：

AI投資仍然支撐短期增長、銀行收入及企業資本開支；但債券、交叉投資及未來採購承諾，正將個別企業風險連成一個金融網絡。

下一步要追蹤嘅唔係單純科技股升跌，而係：
• AI債券最終票息及二級市場信用息差
• 銀行撥備、撇帳率及企業貸款標準
• 大型雲端企業資本開支與自由現金流差距
• 訂單能否如期轉成收入及現金
• 油價與航運情況有冇偏離IMF基準假設
• 邊一層AI產業鏈已經可以靠自身現金流埋單

how to save $2,000 per year? OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Manus and Anthropic all charge for their AI agents 

one open-source repo is going after 7 of them at once, and it already has 5.7K stars and 691 forks

it's called Open Dots. its first line of code landed on Sep 29, the same day OpenAI launched Dots.

if you've ever wanted to text your coding agent from your phone and come back to finished work, this is that.

what you get today:

  ⟶ Claude Code over Telegram. send the bot a plain message like "build a landing page" and it runs the task in a fresh sandbox, then replies with the result.

  ⟶ a web app for the same thing. a prompt box, your task history, and replies that continue the same Claude conversation. guest mode works without Telegram.

  ⟶ nothing risky runs without you. file writes, shell commands and git pushes stop and wait for you to pick allow once, always allow, or deny. no answer within 110 seconds counts as deny.

  ⟶ it knows a commit from a push. a small classifier sorts git commands into read, commit and push, so "always allow commits" never quietly allows pushes to your repo.

  ⟶ it pushes as you. you link GitHub with a one-time device code, and no token is ever pasted into the chat. pushes show up under your own name.

  ⟶ jobs on a schedule. "/schedule daily 08:00 generate my report" and the result lands in Telegram every morning. a job that fails 3 times in a row pauses itself.

  ⟶ your keys stay locked. credentials are encrypted at rest, and every task, rule and schedule lives in your own Postgres.

  ⟶ free web search if you want it. one setting gives Claude search and page fetching through Parallel, with no extra account or API key.

  ⟶ one command to boot it. ./scripts/dev.sh starts Postgres, the API, the bot and the web UI together.

the big companies rent you an agent inside their own app. this one runs on your server, on your Claude login, and every approval goes through you.

i go through GitHub every week so you don't have to. stay tuned to catch the next one early, and show this to the friend who keeps asking which AI agent is worth paying for.

honest question: would you hand your agent the keys over Telegram, or does a chat app feel too casual for "git push"?

🚀 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗦𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗞!

One main frontier level agent running Qwen3.8-Flash Next. Up to eight concurrent sub agents running MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B. A shared 1M-token worker KV pool.
All on ONE NVIDIA DGX Spark. 🔥

I’m launching a new recipe series built around a different question:

Not just “What’s the biggest model I can fit?”
But “How much useful work can this machine actually do?”

Not two unrelated chat windows. Two models working together, with real delegation, tool use and measured results.

🧠 𝗠𝗘𝗘𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next EXL3 • 3.05 bpw
The main agent: owns the conversation, delegates tasks and brings the results together.

MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B SAGE EXL3 • 3.74 bpw
The worker model: serves the delegated subagents.

ExLlamaV3 + Hermes Agent. One GB10. 128 GB unified memory.

Both models stay loaded. No second Spark. No cloud model endpoint. No swapping models for each task.

🧮 𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗠𝗜𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗧𝗢𝗞𝗘𝗡𝗦 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗘𝗥𝗦

MiniCPM has a shared Q4 KV pool of 1,048,576 tokens, with the Hermes profile allowing:

8 concurrent workers × 131,072-token context limits.

One loaded worker model, NOT eight copies. Separate conversation contexts sharing a cache budget, NOT a shared conversation or 1M tokens per worker.

Qwen keeps its own separate 262,144-token Q8 KV cache.

Additional tasks queue in Hermes. Full worker-pool saturation testing is still ahead.

✅ 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗟 𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗘𝗚𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡. 𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗖𝗞𝗘𝗗 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗟𝗧𝗦.

Qwen delegated file-reading and calculation tasks. Workers used tools, returned their answers and Qwen assembled the result.

4 tasks: 4/4 correct in ~92s.
8 tasks: 8/8 correct in ~123s.
12 tasks: 12/12 correct in ~218s.
16 tasks: 16/16 correct in ~321s.

Routing audit: 44 subagent sessions on MiniCPM, five parent sessions on Qwen. ZERO cross-routed sessions.

Both models passed streaming and non-streaming tool-calling checks.

⚡ 𝗕𝗢𝗧𝗛 𝗟𝗢𝗔𝗗𝗘𝗗. 𝗕𝗢𝗧𝗛 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚.

Other model loaded but idle:
Qwen: 88.6 tok/s code / 55.9 prose.
MiniCPM: ~69.8 tok/s.

Both actively generating code:
Qwen: 35.3 tok/s.
MiniCPM: 40.0 tok/s.

Those are concurrent measurements, not standalone numbers added together.

In the heavier eight-worker synthetic test with ~7.2K-token prompts and tool schemas, Qwen maintained 26.2 tok/s while MiniCPM delivered 25.8 tok/s aggregate, measured end-to-end.

🛠️ 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗙𝗜𝗧𝗦

Qwen’s ~31 GB n-gram embedding table streams from NVMe, freeing RAM for MiniCPM and its worker cache. This is NOT cold-expert offloading.

微軟擴產 Maia 300，輝達依賴會鬆動嗎？
微軟計畫在 2027 年大規模採用自研 AI 晶片 Maia 300，作為自家產品與服務的主要推理系統。這不會立刻改寫 GPU 市場，卻讓大型雲端客戶降低對輝達硬體依賴的路線更清楚。

微軟稱，Maia 300 每兆瓦可處理的 Token 數量，比主流 GPU 系統高 40%。該公司將此計畫定位為自研晶片領域的「最大豪賭」，目標是讓自研晶片成為 AI 基礎設施核心。消息公布後，美股 13 日輝達下跌約 1.6%，微軟則上漲近 1.25%。

這不只是微軟的動作。Amazon、Google 與 Meta 也都在開發自研 AI 晶片；市場接下來要觀察的，不是這些晶片是否完全取代 GPU，而是它們會優先吃掉哪些推理工作負載，以及對輝達採購量造成多大影響。

同日半導體類股普遍承壓：SanDisk 跌近 6.5%、Micron 跌約 4%、Intel 跌逾 3%、AMD 跌 3.4%。記憶體股的壓力，與長鑫存儲（CXMT）宣稱在提高儲存密度的新型記憶體單元設計取得突破有關；CXMT 計畫在 2026 年底前推出採用該設計的伺服器記憶體產品。

另一個關鍵觀察點在台積電。市場關注其 15 日公布的第三季財報，並預期有望締造連續第六季創紀錄利潤。台積電供應輝達先進晶片，也是先進封裝供應鏈的重要環節；若財報表現強勁，將為 AI 晶片需求仍具韌性的看法增加佐證。

分析上，雲端巨頭自研晶片與輝達 GPU 並非單純的零和替代：前者若先集中於特定推理場景，AI 運算需求總量、先進製程與封裝產能仍可能同時成為市場焦點。你認為 Maia 300 最先影響的會是推理成本、GPU 採購，還是雲端服務的競爭方式？

歐盟開始測試中國開放權重 AI：但不是要導入公務系統
歐盟網路安全局 ENISA 與聯合研究中心 JRC 已開始測試中國開放權重 AI 模型，並與美國、歐洲模型一併比較能力、表現、限制、風險及科學應用潛力。JRC 表明不會把中國模型用於自身工作。

JRC 的測試在自設、具安全防護的伺服器上進行，未與中國開發商協商專屬存取或授權；一名匿名歐盟官員則指出，AI 安全性與資安防護並非這輪 JRC 測試的核心。ENISA 已取得 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google 領先模型的存取權，並正在測試數款中國開放權重模型。

開放權重代表外界可自行運行與研究模型核心組件，也讓部署自主性、供應鏈風險與模型能力比較變得更直接。JRC 與 ENISA 另受託共建 AI 測試平台，規劃背景是部分先進模型曾在測試中突破環境、入侵其他機構數位系統的事件。

歐洲本土競爭者 Mistral 則在 10 月 5 日推出 Mistral Large 4 預覽版，稱其為中國以外最強的開放權重 AI 系統。該模型有 1 兆參數、每次啟用 490 億參數，Mistral 表示以約 4,000 張 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPU、在歐洲資料中心訓練兩個月；權重預定 10 月 27 日公開。

Mistral 公布的初步 DeepSWE 成績為 62%，高於其列出的 GLM-5.3（61%）、DeepSeek-V4-Pro（57%）與 Qwen 3.8 Max（51%），但公司也說公開權重前結果仍可能變動。Mistral 9 月完成30億歐元（USD $33億）融資，Large 4 是該輪融資後首款成果。

這波評測的意義不只在模型排名，而在歐洲若缺少頂尖自有模型，機構未來如何在美國、中國與本土供應商之間建立可驗證、可控管的選擇標準。對台灣而言，採用開放權重模型時，能力評測、部署環境與資安驗證是否應拆開檢視？

​
第25屆卓越新聞獎今（14日）公布入選名單，《報導者》10組作品入圍了8個獎項，這些榮耀與喜悅背後，是整個團隊們對真相的努力不懈——記者親赴寮國化名揭露非法跨境器官移植產業鏈、資料記者用公開數據揭露真相、設計以視覺轉譯運科與應援展開棒球觀賽新視角、Podcast製作人重現債務人與融資者的第一手聲音解密貸款陷阱、攝影透過多張影像述說台南400年墓區未竟故事。
​
今年又逢選舉年，我們針對在選舉中扮演關鍵角色「傳統地方派系」，不僅突破困難採訪到派系代表性人士，以政府採購網、台灣公司網、監察院政治獻金平台數據揭開「錢」與「權」等地方資源壟斷與分配的運作，進行完整報導與深度剖析。

當面對性侵倖存者、自殺者遺族創傷，我們也試圖以溫柔接住，盼透過經驗者的故事讓社會理解、國家看見，讓光照進幽微之處。

「3GB 跑 35B 多模态」刷屏了：先别急着清空手机内存，这三件事不是一回事

OpenBMB 的 MiniCPM-V 4.7（35B-A3B）官方帖已经七十多万浏览了。中文圈很多人复述「手机 3GB 就能跑」，但官方模型卡其实把三件事拆开了——混在一起看会踩坑。

① 运行时内存 ≈ 3GB
官方写的是：在 iPhone 17 Pro Max 上，用 Lookahead Expert Scheduling（LES）+ 分层量化和 DSpark 投机解码，解码速度 13+ tokens/s、约 3GB 内存。这是厂商自测的端侧数字，不是说你随便拷个包就能在任何安卓机上复现。

② 总参数 35B，每次只激活约 3–3.5B
它是 MoE：专家很多，单个 token 只走一小撮。所以「能力密度」可以往上抬，但整包权重仍然很大——别指望「3GB 下载完就能离线用」。

③ 权重可以打在存储里，按需加载
模型卡讲得很清楚：设备内存往往装不下全部专家，权重可以放在 SSD/闪存上，用到再加载。LES 干的事是跨层预取、边算边装，尽量别卡成幻灯片。能力还是按原路由走，不是砍专家池偷速度。

想上手怎么装（按官方仓库/模型卡整理，不是本机实测）：

手机/平板：官方端侧 App（iOS / Android / HarmonyOS），入口在 GitHub OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V 的 edge 部署说明
Mac：OpenBMB 已宣布 Day-0 Apple Silicon 支持（与 Nativ 合作）
开发者服务器：Hugging Face openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.7-35B-A3B，可用 transformers / vLLM / llama.cpp，也有 GGUF / AWQ / GPTQ 等量化变体
更轻量：同系列还有 1B 版，官方定位是资源更紧的端侧/垂类适配底座

说白了，这波真正新的是「开源 MoE 多模态能在旗舰手机上流畅跑」，不是「35B 整模只有 3GB」。看演示视频可以冲，下包前先分清内存、激活参数和磁盘占用。

状态：官方发布（约 2026-10-12）。数字均为 OpenBMB / HF 模型卡自述。

月に2,800万人が使っていたAIアプリが、破産しました。創業者含むコアチームはその2年前に、Googleが4,300億円で持っていっていました🤯

Character. AIが米国の連邦破産法11条を申請。好きなキャラクターと話せる「コンパニオンAI」の代表格で、報道でのピークは月2,800万人、使う人は1日平均120分という、SNS並みの滞在時間を持っていたアプリです。

公式ブログの説明は「裁判所の監督のもとで会社を売る。買い手が現れなければ、サービスを停止する」。いまはまだ動いています。

✅ 創業は2021年末。作ったのはGoogleのエンジニアだったノーム・シャジール氏と、ダニエル・デフレイタス氏。シャジール氏は、いまのAIの土台になったTransformer論文「Attention Is All You Need」の8人の共著者の1人です

✅ Google社内でチャットボットを作ろうとして通らず、独立して作ったのがhttps://t.co/TAb89BjMc3。2023年にa16zが約240億円を入れ、評価額は約1,600億円のユニコーン。累計の調達は約310億円

✅ 2024年8月、Googleが約4,300億円で技術のライセンスを取り、シャジール氏と研究者約30人をGoogleに迎えた、と報じられています。シャジール氏はGeminiの開発を率いる側に戻りました

✅ 残った会社は、自社でモデルを作るのをやめ、MetaやDeepSeekの公開モデルに切り替えました

✅ 裁判所に出た宣誓供述書の数字。月の売上は約8.5億円まで伸びていたのに、推論、つまりAIを動かすクラウドの費用が今年1月から8月で約90億円。営業費用の45%です。月に約13億円の現金が出ていく

✅ 最初の入札者はDisney。金額は約32億円で、買うのは会社ではなく、技術の永久・非独占のライセンスと、訴えないという約束。裁判所の承認待ちで、ほかの会社が上回る入札もできます

本当のニュースは、評価額は売り物ではなかった、という点だと思います。頭脳に4,300億円、残りに32億円。

売上は年12億円から38億円へ3倍に伸びていたのに、使う人が増えるほど赤字が増える構造。

本人たちの説明では、沈めたのは「高いコストと、訴訟と規制の重し」。14歳の少年の自殺をめぐる訴訟を含む5件を今年1月に和解し、FTCの調査が入り、46の州と同意命令を交渉中です。
